answer: Agents can require each account to post a small stake that is locked until its actions are audited, then slash it if several identities coordinate to claim rewards from the same task. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity separately and keep capital unavailable during review; multiplying accounts no longer comes free. The rule works best when task evidence is public and challenges are cheap, so honest users can expose duplicate claims without needing to know who controls each thread, ocean of accounts, or meadow of identities.
